report.tagline: A UK money app that started with cheap foreign exchange and grew into a global super-app for banking, cards, savings, trading and travel.
report.simpleSummary: Revolut is a bank in an app. You get a card, an account and can spend in 150+ currencies with low fees, which made it famous with travellers. Over time it added savings, stock and crypto trading, insurance, eSIMs for travel and business accounts. Most features are free, and people pay a monthly plan for extras. After years of waiting, it launched as a full UK bank in 2026, and it is now also live in India.

overview.whatItDoes: Revolut gives people an account, card and app to spend, save, send, invest and travel. Businesses use Revolut Business for accounts, cards and payments. It earns from card fees, currency exchange, subscriptions, interest on deposits and trading.
howItWorks: Download the app, verify ID in minutes and get a virtual card instantly, physical card by post.
Spend abroad at the real exchange rate up to a monthly limit, then pay a small fee on free plans.
Send money to friends, split bills, and pay with Apple Pay or Google Pay.
Save in instant-access accounts, invest in stocks and ETFs, buy crypto and gold.
Pay for a plan (Plus, Premium, Metal, Ultra) to get higher limits, travel insurance, lounge access and more perks.
In India, Revolut offers a multi-currency card and account focused on travel and sending money abroad.
overview.valueProposition: One app for all your money, especially cheap and easy when you travel or deal with other currencies.

businessModel.summary: Revolut earns from many small streams: card fees when you pay, currency exchange margins, monthly plans, interest on customer deposits, and trading and crypto fees. Its trick is low cost: no branches, heavy automation, and selling many products to each customer.

revenueStreams.detail: A small fee paid by shops on every card payment.
Margins above limits and at weekends.
Plus, Premium, Metal and Ultra plans.
Earns on customer deposits held at central banks and in bonds.
Fees on stock, crypto and commodity trading.
Plans and transaction fees from Revolut Business.

businessModel.pricing: UK: Standard free; Plus £3.99 a month; Premium £7.99; Metal £14.99; Ultra £45. Fees for FX above plan limits and at weekends. Business plans from free to higher tiers. India pricing differs.
costDrivers: Compliance, anti-money laundering and fraud prevention
Card production and payment network fees
Expanding into new countries and licences
businessModel.unitEconomics: With about 70 million customers and $6 billion revenue, Revolut earns about $85 a year per customer on average. Its profit before tax was about $2.3 billion, so about $33 profit per customer per year. A free user may earn $20 to 40 a year from card fees and interest; a Metal subscriber earns much more. Costs per customer are low because there are no branches and most support is automated.

howTheyGetUsers: Travel use cases spreading among students and young professionals
Social payments: splitting bills pulls friends in
Expanding into new countries such as India, Mexico and Brazil
whatBringsUsersBack: Daily card spending and instant notifications
growth.moat: Revolut's moat is scale plus low cost plus product range. With 70 million users, licences in many countries and one tech stack, it can launch features worldwide cheaply. The more products a user takes, the harder it is to leave. Banks can copy features, but not easily their costs.

northStar.metric: Monthly customers who use Revolut as their main account (salary in, daily spending)
northStar.why: Main account users bring the most value and revenue. It shows trust and daily value, not just sign-ups. This north star metric ties both together. Guardrail metrics make sure growth does not come at the cost of trust, safety or margins.

pmLessons: Start with one sharp hook. Cheap FX for travellers brought users in before Revolut added everything else.
Cross-selling builds value. Each extra product raises revenue per user and makes leaving harder.
Regulation is product work. The long wait for a UK licence limited what Revolut could offer.
Growth needs trust. Frozen accounts and support problems can undo the value of great features.
Low costs are a strategy. No branches lets Revolut serve millions profitably.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you get UK users to make Revolut their main bank now it has a full licence?
interviewQuestions.hint: Barriers: trust, salary switching, features. Ideas: switching service, deposit protection messaging, rewards. Measure salary deposits.

interviewQuestions.question: Revolut has too many features. How would you decide what to show on the home screen?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users. Use data on use. Personalise. Test with A/B. Track engagement and confusion.

interviewQuestions.question: Design Revolut's entry into India.
interviewQuestions.hint: Choose target: travellers and students. Check rules (LRS, RBI). Compare with Niyo and Scapia. Define metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce account freeze complaints without letting fraud in?
interviewQuestions.hint: Balance safety and experience. Better risk models, clear communication, faster review. Track both fraud and complaints.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Revolut launch a free plan with all features to grow faster?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare subscription revenue loss with growth. Look at what drives plan upgrades. Suggest tests.
